findings.title: A single cached birthplace file causes incomplete or stale matching stages to be accepted as complete
findings.what_the_code_does: In MATCHING/_matching_master_dofile.do:75, the existence check 'local built : dir `\"`fsdir'divided_file`y'_fs_cleaned\"' files \"norace*.dta\"' treats the divided files stage as complete if ANY norace*.dta file is present, skipping 1b_fs_divided_files.do even if an interrupted run produced only 1 of 143 birthplaces. In MATCHING/2_ABE_matchingV3_christian_torben.do:81-86, race3_bpl_list is derived from whatever files exist in datadirA. Line 99 uses 'capture mkdir' without clearing existing contents, and MATCHING/3_append_and_clean_all_links_christian_torbenV2.do:73-82 loops over all existing files in that directory. An interrupted or re-executed run thus silently matches a partial birthplace subset or appends obsolete links from prior executions.
findings.why_it_matters: An interrupted build or modified run silently produces an incomplete or corrupted link dataset without throwing an error, distorting overall linkage counts and sample composition.

findings.how_to_check: In the generated link file link1930_1940_fs1930_1940_cleaned_noraceblock0.dta, tabulate fs_used1930 and fs_used1940. Verify the share of candidate links where neither side, or only one side, used a FamilySearch transcription versus Ancestry fallback.
findings.suggested_fix: Document and interpret the FamilySearch baseline as an operational fallback policy rather than a pure FamilySearch transcription benchmark. In empirical analyses, report link rates stratified by fs_used indicators (both sides FS, one side FS, neither side FS), and construct a balanced complete-case sample restricted to records where FamilySearch transcriptions were successfully linked and cleaned on both sides.
findings.title: FamilySearch benchmark falls back to Ancestry names on unlinked or uncleaned records, producing a selective hybrid sample
findings.what_the_code_does: In MATCHING/0b_create_fs_names.do:91, 1930 FamilySearch records are merged with final1930.dta using keep(3), retaining only records already linked to Ancestry histids and dropping ambiguous histids. In MATCHING/1b_fs_divided_files.do:42-56, records start from Ancestry divided files; fs_namefrst_cleaned and fs_namelast_cleaned overwrite Ancestry values only when non-empty, falling back to Ancestry independently for each name field. Exact ABE matching is then run on these hybrid names. The primary link dataset therefore contains pairs linked on Ancestry-Ancestry, Ancestry-FamilySearch, and FamilySearch-FamilySearch combinations.
findings.why_it_matters: The resulting linkage rate is not the effect of substituting FamilySearch transcription for Ancestry. It reflects an endogenous combination of FamilySearch-Ancestry linkability, transcription availability, field-level fallback, and name difficulty. Attributing this link rate to FamilySearch transcription quality conflates transcription accuracy with fallback selection.

Vendor abeclean.ado into replication/stata/ or ensure replication/config.do explicitly sets adopath to its location.
findings.title: FamilySearch linkage pipeline is omitted from master replication runners and input manifests, and lacks dependency setup
findings.what_the_code_does: The FamilySearch matching pipeline is reachable only via an ad-hoc manual invocation documented in a comment at MATCHING/_matching_master_dofile.do:10. Neither replication/run_machineA.do nor any replication runner executes it. Its raw inputs (familysearch_census1930/p1.dta..p126.dta and final1930.dta) are omitted from replication/input_manifest.md and preflight validation. In addition, MATCHING/1b_fs_divided_files.do:51 calls abeclean without setting adopath or configuring the package dependency.
findings.why_it_matters: An independent replicator running the replication suite cannot reproduce the FamilySearch link files or downstream estimates. A standalone execution will fail if external files or unvendored Stata ado dependencies are absent from the environment.

findings.title: Asymmetric matching runs ignore name_type_B and reference invalid paths under locations 2 and 3
findings.what_the_code_does: MATCHING/2_ABE_matchingV3_christian_torben.do introduces name_type_B for asymmetric matching (e.g., matching _fs_cleaned in 1930 to _ans_cleaned in 1940). While location 1 sets datadirB using name_type_B (line 47), location 2 (line 58) and location 3 (line 70) construct datadirB using name_type. Additionally, MATCHING/_matching_master_dofile.do:70 sets fsdir using REP_F, which is undefined outside hostname ARTS-ECON-CM, and line 28 points to a nonexistent local path.
findings.why_it_matters: Running an asymmetric cross-source match under location 2 or 3 reads the incorrect dataset B directory, linking against the wrong name type while mislabeling the output. Using locations other than 1 in _matching_master_dofile.do fails due to undefined or invalid directory paths.

review_limits: No paper draft was supplied, so claims-vs-code could not be assessed against manuscript text, tables, or claims.
The external census microdata (FamilySearch raw files on F: and intermediate link files) could not be processed at scale, as the Stata pipeline cannot be run in this environment.
Runtime performance, execution time, and empirical link rates are inferred from static source analysis rather than pipeline execution.
The review target was strictly the uncommitted working-tree changes in MATCHING/; pre-existing ABE matching algorithms (e.g. abematch.ado) were not audited.
structured_output.summary: The FamilySearch matching extension implements strict merge assertions and clean field fallback, but its caching logic permits partially built birthplace directories and stale link outputs to be silently accepted as complete. The resulting benchmark is an endogenous FamilySearch/Ancestry hybrid rather than a pure FamilySearch comparison, which will distort linkage evaluation unless stratified by the supplied source indicators. The workflow is not yet integrated into the repository's replication runner or input manifest, and fails to handle asymmetric runs outside location 1.

summary.description: Two to four sentences. The overall state of the reviewed work and the single most important thing to fix. No preamble.

dimensions_reviewed.description: Which scope dimensions were actually reviewed in this run.

findings.description: Defects and concerns, ordered most severe first. Empty if none. Do not pad with stylistic observations.

severity.description: blocker: a reported result is wrong. major: a referee would demand it. minor: real but survivable. nit: cosmetic.

confidence.description: verified: traced in the source. likely: strongly implied but depends on unseen data. speculative: a question, not an established defect.

title.description: One line, stating the defect itself, not its category.

location.description: path:line, or path:line-line. Several may be comma-separated. Required: a finding without a location is not a finding.

what_the_code_does.description: Precisely what the code computes, quoting the relevant expression. Contrast with what it was evidently intended to compute.

why_it_matters.description: The consequence for a number or claim in the paper. If there is no consequence, the severity is nit.

how_to_check.description: A concrete command, tabulation, or count the author can run to confirm or refute this in minutes.

suggested_fix.description: The change, specific enough to act on. Do not apply it yourself.

verified_clean.description: Things explicitly checked that were fine. This is what makes a short findings list trustworthy rather than lazy.

evidence.description: How it was confirmed, with path:line where applicable.

review_limits.description: What this review could NOT establish: data not readable, pipeline not runnable, paper text unavailable, Stata semantics not verifiable by reading. Be explicit; silence here reads as false assurance.
